newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand bows out bruised, bonds trudge along.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand bows out bruised, bonds trudge along.

text.p: The South African rand ended Thursday's official dealings a battered unit on strong offshore demand for steadily strengthening dollars.
The rand was last changing hands at 4.6850/6880 to the dollar from Wednesday's closing level of 4.6585/6615.
"There was some good demand for dollars from London. Whether it was a specific order or not I can't say. With the dollar moving up against the mark, its not helping the rand," said one forex trader.

Another dealer said: "Jo'burg was caught short (dollars) and ended up having to pay it and its the normal snowball effect. It has been a very thin market so...I don't think a very big amount's gone through, just steady, small amounts."

Players expected the rand to take a run at 4.70 on Friday, especially if the dollar/mark continued to rise, but the local unit was seen limited to 4.6950 at the highest by traditional pre-weekend book squaring activity.
"The next level is really close to the 4.70s again. It has been in this wide range of 4.65 to 4.70 so there's not much protecting it from running near to 4.70," said one dealer.
The rand missed joining the dollar in its afternoon assault on the mark, ending at 0.3930/3936 from 0.3936/3940 late Wednesday.
Rand/yen was stronger at 25.0288/0662 from 24.7833/8207. Against sterling, the rand weakened further over the session, last trading at 7.4275/4346 from 7.3543/3637.
Bond yields ground lower in thin, late afternoon action in step with a strong U.S. debt market before nudging back at the official close to stand broadly unchanged.
The bellwether R150 long bond was last at 14.03 percent, unchanged from Wednesday's close. The R150 hit its intraday best level of 13.98 percent around 0715 GMT.
"It's been very thin all day and I think the market's exhausted after doing so well over the week," said one bond dealer.
Debt market torpor was expected to continue into Friday, which sees the maturity and payment of final coupons on the government's R119 gilt.
The Reserve Bank said on Wednesday the money market shortage could decline substantially after the maturity but the market will have to wait until next week to see the statistics.
In the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 to 14.95 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 9.068 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.589 billion rand on Tuesday.
Foreigners sold 68.81 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying a net 324.38 million rands worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover totalled 10.202 billion on Wednesday, rising from 8.056 billion rand on Tuesday.
